summary: Stanislas Julien was a French scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Lycée Pothier and the Collège de France under Abel-Rémusat. He held the Chair of Chinese at the Collège de France (1832–1873).

Stanislav Grof studied at Charles University (ca. 1950–1956). His career included posts at Johns Hopkins University (1967–1969), the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center (1969–1973), Esalen Institute (1973–1987), and the California Institute of Integral Studies (1994–2015).
Stanislav Mudra was an Indologist. He completed his Ph.D. at the Faculty of Arts, Charles University in Prague, studying under doctoral supervisor Otakar Pertold from around 1929 to 1936.
Stanislav Šmelhaus was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý between circa 1907 and 1925.

Stanisław Franciszek Michalski was an Indologist. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Vienna under Leopold von Schroeder and Paul Kretschmer, later studying at Göttingen. From 1945 to 1960, he served as a lecturer at the University of Łódź.

Stanisław Schayer was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Freiburg under Leumann and Husserl, completed his habilitation at Lviv under Gawroński, and served as professor at the University of Warsaw from 1929.
Stanley Abe is a scholar in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held academic posts at Duke University, where his presence is attested in 1995 and 2004.

Stanley Cecil Sutton worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as librarian at the Commonwealth Relations Office (attested 1953) and later at the India Office Records (attested 1974).

Stanley Insler was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian-Central Asian studies scholar. After studying at Columbia, Tübingen, and Yale under Paul Thieme and Karl Hoffmann, he served as Edward E. Salisbury Professor at Yale University from ca. 1978 to 2012.

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Ceylon and Cornell, he taught at Cambridge and Chicago before serving as Professor of Anthropology at Harvard University (1976–2001).

Stanley Lombardo works in linguistics and philosophy. He was educated at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin, and held a post at the University of Kansas from circa 1976 to 2014.

Stanley Weinstein was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and taught at SOAS University of London (ca. 1962–1968) and Yale University from 1968.

Stanley Wolpert was a historian and Indologist. Educated at the City College of New York and the University of Pennsylvania, he served as an assistant professor, associate professor, and department chair at the University of California, Los Angeles, beginning in 1959.
Stefan Anacker was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison between circa 1965 and 1970, studying under Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who completed his dissertation at the University of Washington. He has held lead researcher posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (ca. 2012).

Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Leopold von Schroeder, Richard Simon, Antoine Meillet, and Sylvain Lévi. He succeeded Andrzej Gawroński as professor at the University of Lviv, serving from 1928 to 1941.

Stefan Larsson specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Stockholm University in 2009 under Per-Arne Berglie, later working as a researcher at Stockholm University, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, and senior lecturer at the University of Gävle.

Stefan Mario Maul is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He earned degrees from Göttingen and Freie Universität Berlin, and in 1995 he became Ordinarius for Assyriology at Heidelberg University.

Stefan Mladenov was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Sofia, Vienna, Saint Petersburg, and Charles University, where he earned a Ph.D. He subsequently served as professor of linguistics at Sofia University from 1919.

Stefania Travagnin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen (ca. 2013–2020) and held a post at SOAS University of London around 2020.
